newsitem.title: Italy: SOCCER-BAGGIO BACK TO HIS BEST AS ITALY BEAT POLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAGGIO BACK TO HIS BEST AS ITALY BEAT POLAND.

text.p: Roberto Baggio made a winning return to international soccer on Wednesday with the goal of the night as Italy swept aside Poland 3-0 in a World Cup European group two qualifier.
"I did not want to let down the people of Naples," the ponytailed AC Milan midfielder said.

Dropped by former Italy coach Arrigo Sacchi in late 1995 and with his future at Milan looking uncertain after failing to secure a regular first team place, the Baggio of old dodged defenders to score a superb 63rd minute goal.
He had been on the pitch only 12 minutes after coming on in the 51st minute as a replacement for Gianfranco Zola, who had been a doubtful starter because of a muscle strain.
Baggio weaved into the area, drew goalkeeper Andrzej Wozniak off his line and then shot home.

The goal was the last of the match and maintained Italy's place at the top of the group, unbeaten on 16 points and ahead of England on 12 with a game in hand. Poland's chances look dim with just four points from four matches.
Italy, who drew 0-0 with Poland in Chorzow earlier in the month, have also not conceded a goal since veteran Cesare Maldini took over from Sacchi in January.
Baggio did not speak of Sacchi, with whom he fell out after the coach returned to Milan last December, but was clearly convinced the good times were coming back.
Maldini thanked Baggio at a later news conference. "He showed that he is a truly great player," he said.
Maldini would not be drawn on whether Baggio could now expect to be a regular face in the team again.
"I never make long term plans. When I needed a player like Baggio I called him up," he said. He answered excellently. Now we'll see."
Chelsea midfielder Roberto Di Matteo had opened the scoring with his first international goal in the 23rd minute -- a half-volleyed shot from a Demetrio Albertini cross.
After the goal, the game improved with Italy growing in confidence and the crowd roaring them on.
"They were really the 12th man. The public was marvellous," said Maldini of the 35,000-strong crowd.
Zola hit the crossbar in the 25th minute and could have scored again in the 32nd when he was sent through clear on goal but was blocked by Wozniak.
Captain Paolo Maldini, playing his 80th match for Italy, made it 2-0 in the 37th minute with a scooped shot into the back of the net after a flicked-on header from Ciro Ferrara.
Wozniak blocked Maldini's first shot but the son of coach Cesare, who himself made his international debut in Naples 37 years ago, got the rebound at the far post.
It was Maldini's fifth goal for Italy and his second in the four matches played under his father's guidance.

Polnd had a chance of a consolation goal near the end when Krzysztof Warzycha had a clear sight of goal with only goalkeeper Angelo Peruzzi to beat. The Juventus goalkeeper, who had a quiet night, blocked the shot with his legs.
